title: The fixed scalar/open restriction mate respects the normalized tensor comparisons
statement: For arbitrary commutative rings A and B in Type (u+1), a ring homomorphism φ:A→B, schemes U and X in universe u, and an open immersion j:U→X, let F_T be the fixed derived scalar extension, G_A and G_B the exact derived restrictions, r:G_A;F_U≅F_X;G_B the fixed scalar/restriction mate of [lem-coef-etale-open-comparison-data], δ_A and δ_B its exact restriction tensor isomorphisms, and t_T the uniquely normalized scalar tensor comparisons of [lem-coef-etale-hom-thick-locus]. For all K,M in D(X_et,A), F_U(δ_A(K,M));r_(K tensor M);G_B(t_X(K,M)^(-1)) = t_U(G_A K,G_A M)^(-1);(r_K tensor id);(id tensor r_M);δ_B(F_X K,F_X M). Both are maps from F_U(G_A K tensor G_A M) to G_B(F_X K tensor F_X M). There is no boundedness, flat coefficient-map, constructibility or quasi-compactness hypothesis.

source.place: The coefficient-tensor compatibility for extension by zero, reduced to the ordinary monoidal scalar/restriction square; Stacks sites-modules.tex Tags 03EL and 0E8J, sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YY and 07A4.

proof.text: Identify the scalar tensor comparison used by etaleHomTensorComparison with the inverse of ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorIso. The latter satisfies its all-complex representative normalization; restrict this normalization to flat-term K-flat pairs using site_normalization_flat. Its inverse family is natural in both arguments by productIso_natural1 and productIso_natural2. Uniqueness in etaleHomTensorComparison_existsUnique identifies the families, hence their inverse components.

Identify openScalarRestriction with the inverse normalized scalarPullbackIso transported along the exact/left-derived restriction isomorphisms. The identity between the ordinary restriction-of-coefficients square and the canonical geometric square gives the derived square identity. The inverse-mate transport formula then gives the comparison map. The normalized inverse mate equals scalarPullbackIso by scalarPullback_eq. Unfolding openExactRestrictionTensor expresses it as transport of the inverse leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso; naturality of the curried tensor interchanges the two independent exact/left-derived comparison maps.

Apply etaleScalarPullback_tensor to j, K and M. Rotate its six invertible arrows by cancellation to orient the square from scalar extension of the restricted tensor to restriction of the scalar-extended tensor. Transport through the exact/left-derived restriction isomorphisms. Naturality of the scalar tensor comparison moves the two A-comparison maps, and naturality of the B-comparison moves the scalar tensor map. Functoriality on the product category cancels the B-comparison maps with their inverses. Substitute the identifications from the preceding steps and expand the uncurried tensor map into its two curried factors. This gives exactly the displayed equation, with every fixed map and every input unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleOpenScalarRestrictionTensor
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (K M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) :
    (scalarExtension φ U).map
        (openExactRestrictionTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j K M).hom ≫
      (openScalarRestriction φ j).hom.app
        (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj K).obj M) ≫
      (derivedRestriction (A := B) j).map (etaleHomTensorComparison X φ K M).inv =
    (etaleHomTensorComparison U φ
        ((derivedRestriction (A := A) j).obj K)
        ((derivedRestriction (A := A) j).obj M)).inv ≫
      ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) U).map
        ((openScalarRestriction φ j).hom.app K)).app
          ((scalarExtension φ U).obj ((derivedRestriction (A := A) j).obj M)) ≫
      ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) U).obj
        ((derivedRestriction (A := B) j).obj ((scalarExtension φ X).obj K))).map
          ((openScalarRestriction φ j).hom.app M) ≫
      (openExactRestrictionTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) j
        ((scalarExtension φ X).obj K) ((scalarExtension φ X).obj M)).hom
